findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot handle audit-log datetime values
findings.description:
`OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `get_item_key()` applies `math.floor()` or `math.ceil()` directly to a Python `datetime`. Any nonempty optimized response therefore raises `TypeError` while building its cursors. Subsequent cursor values also lack the timestamp-to-datetime conversion implemented by `DateTimePaginator`.

Inherit the datetime cursor behavior rather than the numeric behavior, and add endpoint tests covering nonempty results and forward/backward navigation with `optimized_pagination=true`.

findings.title: Unconditional member access breaks organization-level API authentication
findings.description:
`RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is explicitly optional. Organization-level API authentication can pass the endpoint’s scope checks without an associated organization member, but this expression dereferences `member.has_global_access` whenever the user is not a superuser.

Because the expression is evaluated even when `optimized_pagination` is absent, existing ordinary audit-log requests using such authentication now return 500. Evaluate eligibility only when requested and guard the optional membership. Add regression coverage for organization-level API credentials.

findings.title: Negative queryset slicing does not provide advanced pagination
findings.description:
Django querysets reject negative slice indices; they do not handle them as reverse-pagination boundaries. With advanced features enabled, a cursor such as `0:-1:0` reaches `queryset[-1:100]` and raises `ValueError`. `Endpoint.paginate()` only translates `BadPaginationError`, so this becomes a 500 rather than a controlled client error.

Reject negative offsets with `BadPaginationError`, or implement reverse traversal through supported ordering and cursor predicates. Add negative-offset tests for both navigation directions.

findings.title: Sorted-set conversion reuses keys containing ordinary Redis sets
findings.description:
The new `ZADD` and `ZSCAN` operations use the same `span-buf:s:*` keys previously populated by `SADD`. Existing buffered segments therefore cause Redis `WRONGTYPE` errors during ingestion or flushing after deployment. During a rolling deployment, old and new consumers can also encounter each other’s incompatible key types. The Lua script’s replacement of set commands with sorted-set commands has the same incompatibility.

Provide a compatible transition, such as a versioned namespace with handling for draining the old buffers, or explicit support for both representations. Add tests that seed legacy set-backed segments before exercising ingestion and flushing.
